original_question: Let X be a compact Kahler manifold, or more generally a manifold in the Fujiki class, and let omega be a smooth semi-positive big (1,1)-form. If phi belongs to the finite-energy class E(X, omega), determine whether phi has zero Lelong number at every point.
target_in_paper: Question 36 (Berman-Boucksom-Eyssidieux-Guedj-Zeriahi) in §5.3, “Lelong numbers of finite energy currents.” ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct ambient setting (compact Kähler manifold, with the paper also allowing manifolds in the Fujiki class), the correct positivity hypothesis on ω (smooth, semi-positive, big), the correct class E(X,ω), and the correct conclusion to be tested (vanishing of all Lelong numbers). In substance, it is very close to the paper’s official formulation. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
missing_details: The paper states explicitly that φ is an ω-plurisubharmonic function, i.e. φ ∈ PSH(X,ω), not just an unnamed element of E(X,ω). ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

To make the question stand-alone, one should define “big” exactly as the paper does here: if n = dim_C X, then ∫_X ω^n > 0. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

The notation E(X,ω) should be unpacked using §2.1: with V := ∫_X ω^n and MA(φ) := V^{-1}⟨(ω+dd^cφ)^n⟩, one has E(X,ω) = {φ ∈ PSH(X,ω) : MA(φ) is a probability measure}. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
The quantifier should be explicit: the question asks whether ν(φ,x) = 0 for every point x ∈ X. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

Paper-faithfully, this is posed as an open question (“Is it true that ...?”), not as a solved determination problem. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

Nearby context clarifies that the genuinely delicate part is the boundary of the ample locus Amp({ω}); on Amp({ω}) the known Kähler-type argument works, and Theorem 5.2 gives a special positive case coming from resolutions of singularities. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
refined_question: Let X be a compact Kähler manifold, or more generally a compact complex manifold in the Fujiki class, of complex dimension n, and let ω be a smooth semi-positive big (1,1)-form, meaning ∫_X ω^n > 0. For φ ∈ PSH(X,ω), write V := ∫_X ω^n and MA(φ) := V^{-1}⟨(ω+dd^cφ)^n⟩, where ⟨(ω+dd^cφ)^n⟩ denotes the non-pluripolar Monge-Ampère product; define the finite-energy class E(X,ω) := {φ ∈ PSH(X,ω) : MA(φ) is a probability measure}. If φ ∈ E(X,ω), is it true that the Lelong number ν(φ,x) vanishes for every x ∈ X? ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper’s official Question 36 in §5.3, not a broader neighboring problem. I refined it only by making explicit the definitions that the paper uses implicitly nearby: E(X,ω) is defined in §2.1 via full non-pluripolar Monge-Ampère mass, and the surrounding discussion in §5.3 explains that the known proof covers the Kähler case and points of the ample locus, while Theorem 5.2 gives the special desingularization case. This keeps the question narrow and faithful to the paper’s actual intent. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
